2026 Third Quarter - Core Operations:

Revenue of $6.0 billion, 7.2% organic growth
Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITA of $1.1 billion, 18.2% margin
2026 Third Quarter - Reported:

Revenue of $6.4 billion
Diluted earnings per share of $2.38; $2.73 Non-GAAP Adjusted, up 22%
Operating Income of $991.7 million; $1.1 billion Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITA, 17.6% margin
NEW YORK, Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Omnicom (NYSE: OMC) today announced results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

"As we approach the one-year anniversary of the Interpublic acquisition, we continue to deliver the expected benefits of the combination. We've strengthened our competitive position and are on track to deliver $900 million in cost-reduction synergies in 2026 resulting in stronger organic revenue growth, operating margins, and earnings per share," said John Wren, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Omnicom. "With our integration nearly complete and our portfolio of companies and operations streamlined, we're focused on high-demand services and are well positioned to pursue future growth. We'll continue investing in our people and agentic technology to drive measurable business outcomes for our clients."

Revenue from Core Operations
Revenue from Core Operations in the third quarter of 2026 increased $407.4 million, or 7.3%, to $6.0 billion as compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to organic growth of $400.8 million, or 7.2%, and an increase due to foreign currency translation of $3.4 million, or 0.1%.

Revenue contribution by discipline as a percentage of revenue from Core Operations of $6.0 billion in the third quarter of 2026 was as follows: $3.2 billion, or 53.0%, for Integrated Media; $935.4 million, or 15.6%, for Advertising; $566.6 million, or 9.4%, for Health; $678.3 million, or 11.3%, for Public Relations; and $644.3 million, or 10.7%, for Experiential & Other. Revenue from dispositions and assets held for sale was $412.1 million.

Revenue contribution by region as a percentage of revenue from Core Operations of $6.0 billion in the third quarter of 2026 was as follows: $3.6 billion, or 60.2%, for the United States; $721.1 million, or 12.0%, for Euro Markets & Other Europe; $555.7 million, or 9.2%, for the United Kingdom; $573.1 million, or 9.6%, for Asia Pacific; $226.8 million, or 3.8%, for Latin America; $145.7 million, or 2.4%, for the Middle East & Africa; and $168.6 million, or 2.8%, for Other North America.

Adjusted EBITA from Core Operations
Adjusted EBITA from Core Operations in the third quarter of 2026 increased $191.1 million, or 21.1%, to $1.1 billion as compared to the third quarter of 2025, and the related margin increased to 18.2% from 16.2%, primarily due to cost reduction synergies and organic revenue growth. For the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, Adjusted EBITA excluded repositioning costs, primarily related to real estate and other exit charges in connection with the acquisition of The Interpublic Group of Companies, Inc. ("IPG") and integration and acquisition-related costs of $125.1 million ($76.8 million after tax) and $99.4 million ($79.2 million after tax), respectively. For the third quarter of 2026, Adjusted EBITA from Core Operations excluded a $106.8 million gain on the disposition of a subsidiary.

Core Operations
Core Operations: calculated from the consolidated revenue, adjusted operating income and adjusted EBITA of Omnicom, excluding results of businesses that have been disposed of up to the date of disposition in 2026 and businesses classified as held for sale. Amounts for 2025 are calculated on a combined basis for Omnicom and IPG.
Revenue
Revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased $2.4 billion to $6.4 billion as compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to the acquisition of IPG, which closed on November 26, 2025, and constant currency revenue growth. Revenue in the third quarter of 2026 includes $412.1 million from dispositions and assets held for sale.

Expenses
Operating expenses increased $1.9 billion to $5.4 billion in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to the acquisition of IPG. Included in operating expenses in the third quarter of 2026 are $40.4 million of integration and transaction costs related to the acquisition of IPG, $84.7 million of repositioning costs, primarily related to real estate and other exit charges, and a $106.8 million gain on the disposition of a subsidiary.

Salary and service costs increased $1.7 billion to $4.6 billion, primarily due to the IPG acquisition and constant currency revenue growth. These costs tend to fluctuate with changes in revenue and are comprised of salary and related costs, which include employee compensation and benefits costs, freelance labor, third-party service costs, and third-party incidental costs. Salary and related costs increased $1.1 billion to $2.9 billion, due to revenue growth and the acquisition of IPG. Third-party service costs increased $552.4 million to $1.5 billion, primarily due to growth in our Integrated Media discipline and the acquisition of IPG. Third-party incidental costs increased $24.3 million to $211.7 million, primarily due to revenue growth and the acquisition of IPG.

Occupancy and other costs, which are less directly linked to changes in revenue than salary and service costs, increased $176.6 million to $499.3 million, primarily due to the acquisition of IPG.

SG&A expenses increased $37.4 million to $200.9 million, primarily due to the acquisition of IPG. Included in SG&A expenses in the third quarter of 2026 are $40.4 million of integration and transaction costs related to the acquisition of IPG, compared to $60.8 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Operating Income
Operating income increased $461.6 million to $991.7 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily as a result of revenue growth and the IPG acquisition, partially offset by costs primarily related to the integration of IPG.

Interest Expense, net
Net interest expense in the third quarter of 2026 increased $61.0 million to $104.2 million compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to debt assumed as part of the IPG acquisition and the refinancing activities in the first quarter of 2026. Interest expense increased $72.4 million to $132.8 million. Interest income increased $11.4 million to $28.6 million.

Income Taxes
Our effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 24.3% compared to 27.2% for the third quarter of 2025. The 2026 effective tax rate included the impacts of favorable settlements of uncertain tax positions. The effective tax rates for 2025 reflect the impact of the lower tax benefit associated with integration costs, severance, and repositioning charges related to the acquisition of IPG. Excluding these items, our Non-GAAP adjusted effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 25.0% compared to 26.0% for the third quarter of 2025.

Net Income – Omnicom Group Inc. and Diluted Net Income per Share
Net Income - Omnicom Group Inc. for the third quarter of 2026 increased $314.7 million to $656.0 million compared to the third quarter of 2025. Weighted-average diluted shares outstanding for the third quarter of 2026 increased to 275.4 million from 194.9 million, primarily as a result of shares issued for the IPG acquisition, partially offset by net share repurchases, including shares purchased pursuant to the accelerated stock repurchase agreement. Diluted net income per share of $2.38 increased by $0.63 from $1.75 in the prior year period.

Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income per Share - Diluted for the third quarter of 2026 increased $0.49, or 21.9%, to $2.73 from $2.24. Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income per Share - Diluted for the third quarters of 2026 and 2025 excluded $88.9 million and $15.9 million, respectively, of after-tax amortization expense. Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income per Share - Diluted for the third quarter of 2026 also excluded $13.3 million of after-tax integration and transaction costs, $63.5 million of after-tax severance and repositioning costs, and a $69.5 million after-tax gain on the disposition of a subsidiary. In 2025, Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income per Share - Diluted excluded $50.8 million of costs related to the acquisition of IPG and $28.4 million of after-tax severance and repositioning costs. We present Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income per Share - Diluted to allow for comparability with the prior year period.

EBITA
EBITA increased $560.2 million to $1,111.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITA increased $479.1 million, or 73.6%, to $1,130.1 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, and the related margin increased to 17.6% from 16.1%. EBITA and Adjusted EBITA excluded amortization expense of $120.1 million and $21.5 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively. Adjusted EBITA in the third quarter of 2026 also excluded $40.4 million of costs related to the integration of IPG, severance and repositioning costs of $84.7 million, and a $106.8 million gain on the disposition of a subsidiary. Adjusted EBITA in the third quarter of 2025 also excluded $60.8 million of costs related to the acquisition of IPG and $38.6 million of severance and repositioning costs.

Risks and Uncertainties
Global economic conditions and disruptions, including geopolitical events, international hostilities, acts of terrorism, public health crises, inflation or stagflation, tariffs and other trade barriers, central bank interest rate policies in countries that comprise our major markets, labor and supply chain issues affecting the distribution of our clients' products, or a disruption in the credit markets could cause economic uncertainty and volatility. The impact of these issues on our business will vary by geographic market and discipline. We monitor economic conditions and disruptions closely, as well as client revenue levels and other factors. In response to reductions in revenue, we can take actions to align our cost structure with changes in client demand and manage our working capital. However, there can be no assurance as to the effectiveness of our efforts to mitigate any impact of the current and future adverse economic conditions and disruptions, reductions in client revenue, changes in client creditworthiness, and other developments.

Definitions - Components of Revenue Change
We use certain terms in describing the components of the change in revenue above.

Core Operations: Revenue from Core Operations excludes businesses that have been disposed of or are classified as held for sale. Amounts for 2025 are calculated on a combined basis for Omnicom and IPG.

Organic growth: calculated by subtracting the foreign exchange rate impact and the acquisition revenue from total revenue growth, which is equal to the current period revenue from Core Operations minus the prior period revenue from Core Operations.

Foreign exchange rate impact on core operations: calculated by translating the current period's local currency revenue using the prior period average exchange rates to derive current period constant currency revenue. The foreign exchange rate impact is the difference between the current period revenue in U.S. Dollars and the current period constant currency revenue.

Percentage change: Calculated by dividing the individual component amount by the prior period Core Operations revenue base.
